question: Should OpenClaw accept currentTokenCount plus these token-budget helpers as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold token budgeting into the broader assemble metadata design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137?
rationale: The patch changes plugin-facing API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against, while the broader assemble metadata direction is still open.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
options.body: Approve currentTokenCount as a separate backward-compatible API, but require message/count alignment, SDK baseline regeneration, and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and land token headroom together with the provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design tracked in the broader RFC.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Allow the assemble parameter direction but remove the new SDK helper exports until maintainers settle the public helper surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
recommendation.body: Approve currentTokenCount as a separate backward-compatible API, but require message/count alignment, SDK baseline regeneration, and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman is assigned and has the most direct recent history on the same context-engine budgeting path.
